title: K31.46 at the pump: the tax holiday ends, excise returns — and Zambia wakes to its steepest fuel-price jump of the year
excerpt: No statutory instrument appeared before midnight, so the six-month fuel-tax relief died on schedule. The Energy Regulation Board's October review restores excise duty and passes on dearer oil and a weaker kwacha: petrol up 24 per cent to K31.46, diesel up 24 to K33.27 — with VAT's return dated for 1 December.
author: Natasha Banda

title: “Instruments of justice and service, not sources of fear”: the Catholic bishops and the CCZ close ranks on the state of the nation
excerpt: In separate but aligned statements on one Wednesday, Zambia's two largest church bodies questioned the credibility of the 2026 elections, decried arbitrary arrests and force that has cost civilian lives, and demanded an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya. October, the bishops declared, will be a month of rosary prayers for peace.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: “The outcome was never in doubt — the process is”: Antonio Mwanza gives the ECZ three questions, and a warning about 2031
excerpt: The Democratic Progressive Party leader accepts that President Hichilema won — and says that is precisely why the Electoral Commission must now account for the suspended count, Mandevu's stolen ballots and a dead election agent. His prescription: commissioners chosen independently, a timetable that binds the incumbent, and public media that covers everyone.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Two hundred and fifty basis points: the Bank of Zambia delivers its biggest cut in more than a decade
excerpt: Economists expected twenty-five. The Monetary Policy Committee delivered two hundred and fifty, taking the policy rate to 10.75 per cent — a fourth consecutive cut, powered by 6.1 per cent inflation, a record maize harvest and a firmer kwacha. The committee's own risk list, though, reads like next month's news.
author: Natasha Banda

title: K212 billion for creditors: the Green Paper prices the new term — and debt service outbids FISP, CDF and free education combined
excerpt: The 2027–2029 Medium-Term Budget Plan, the Treasury's first blueprint of the new mandate, sets aside K212.2 billion for debt service — K63.6 billion more than the entire transfers budget for farmers, constituencies, pupils and school meals. The bill falls as a share of GDP only if the growth promises are true.
author: Natasha Banda

title: The Fund is back in town: Zambia opens successor-programme talks — and wants a deal before the year ends
excerpt: An IMF mission led by Edward Gemayel is in Lusaka until 10 October, negotiating a successor to the US$1.7 billion programme that ended in January. The government is selling growth; the Fund is checking the sustainability file. Both are reading the same Green Paper.
author: Natasha Banda

title: “Not the Judiciary — the security services”: the State's answer for the three days the courts went dark
excerpt: Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha has told the Constitutional Court that August's closure of the courts was ordered by the defence and national security services, and merely communicated by the Judiciary. The admission — the first official attribution of responsibility — comes as the State asks that the Chapter One Foundation petition be dismissed with costs.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Five more carcasses in Nabwalya, twenty-six people on the register: the anthrax response races the river
excerpt: Three more hippos and two more elephants have died of anthrax in the Nabwalya Game Management Area, taking the wildlife toll to 49 hippos, nine elephants and six buffaloes. Twenty-six human cases have now been reported — and investigators keep finding evidence that people are reaching the carcasses first.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: 0.2 seconds at 18:21: ZESCO explains the night Levy Mwanawasa went dark — and promises new lights
excerpt: The blackout that stopped Zambia's 2-0 win over Togo for eighteen minutes lasted, on the utility's account, a fifth of a second. The floodlights simply could not forgive it: their design demands about twenty minutes to return to full brightness. ZESCO will now engage the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts on a redesign.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Ten years of the Lusaka July — in October: “The Tale of a Ruby” opens at the National Museum on the 16th
excerpt: The capital's most dressed-up weekend has a theme, a date and a tenth birthday. Lusaka July 2026 runs 16–18 October across three signature events, opening with a Night of Culture at the Lusaka National Museum — the social season's anchor, transplanted to the year's busiest cultural month.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: Two billion for a Medical City, a challenge for Mopani and a pact still unsigned: Hichilema's US$2.14 billion day in Abu Dhabi
excerpt: Memoranda worth US$2.14 billion were signed at the Zambia-UAE Business Forum on Tuesday, anchored by a US$2 billion plan to build a Medical City in Lusaka. The President also told Mopani's Emirati owners that the three-million-tonne copper target needs more of their ore — and left the biggest document, a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, for another day.
author: Natasha Banda

title: A night at Chimbokaila, a day of paperwork, then a smile at the gate: the Archbishop walks free on bail
excerpt: The Archbishop of Lusaka spent Monday night in the capital's best-known correctional facility while his lawyers worked the bail conditions through the system. Late on Tuesday afternoon the gates opened, and the country's most watched defendant walked out smiling — to high-fives, handshakes and a Church that had barely slept.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Fourteen vacancies, one date: Mandevu, Lumezi North and Mbala vote again on 5 November — with August's ghosts on the ballot
excerpt: The Electoral Commission has set Thursday, 5 November for two parliamentary by-elections, a mayoral race and eleven ward polls across five provinces. Mandevu's fresh vote is the residue of an attack on its own totalling centre; Lumezi North and Mbala are voting because death took their candidates within days of the election.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Sixty-five kwacha in every hundred never came back: government freezes the 2026 CDF loan window and turns collector
excerpt: The empowerment-loan arm of the Constituency Development Fund — the cheap money aimed at youths, women, persons with disabilities and marketeers — is shut for 2026. The ministry says only 35 per cent of what has been lent since 2021 has been repaid, and new borrowers will now be funded only from what defaulters return.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Midnight, and still no signature: the fuel-tax holiday lapses tonight — and the ERB's October numbers follow within hours
excerpt: Unless a statutory instrument appears in the next few hours, the excise suspension and VAT zero-rating that have kept two lines of the pump-price build-up blank since April die at midnight. The October review — the first in six months with the full tax load back in the formula — lands on the same midnight.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Turkish Airlines is leaving Lusaka's map — and an economist says the route is the least of what departs with it
excerpt: The carrier has removed Lusaka from its future schedules for good. Kelvin Chisanga's warning is about what goes with it: investor access, tourist arrivals, and a piece of the country's argument — made again in Abu Dhabi this week — that Zambia is open for business.
author: Natasha Banda

title: K50, sausages and pens: the Lumezi South petition puts a farm linked to the Archbishop inside an election fight
excerpt: The losing UPND candidate in Lumezi South wants a recount or a nullification — and his testimony alleges voters were given money and gifts at a farm associated with Archbishop Alick Banda, with instructions to vote for Brian Mundubile and Oliver Mwale. Under cross-examination, he conceded he has no pictures.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: A US$2 billion city on paper, a Brazilian delegation in the corridor and a mine's K5.7 million: health's week of promises
excerpt: The Medical City memorandum signed in Abu Dhabi is the largest health promise Zambia has ever heard. In the same week, smaller and more provable ones arrived — a pharmaceutical delegation from Brazil, a hospital upgrade from a mine, steady drug stocks in Chipangali. The gap between the two scales is where the health system actually lives.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: Two goals, one blackout and a weight lifted: Zambia beat Togo 2-0 and turn Group I into a contest
excerpt: Albert Kangwanda scored inside three minutes, the floodlights failed for twenty, and Eliya Mandanji finished it in stoppage time. Zambia's first win of the campaign draws them level with Togo on three points — and turns November's double-header with Burundi into the decider it was always going to be.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Free entry, thirty countries, one Saturday: the Diplomatic Fun Fair joins Lusaka's biggest weekend of the year
excerpt: The Ministry of Tourism has launched the 2026 Diplomatic Fun Fair for 3 October at the Lusaka Showgrounds — the same Saturday Jason Derulo headlines the polo fields. For the capital's cultural economy, it is the busiest weekend on record.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: The Archbishop in the dock: Banda denies the Hilux charge, wins K80,000 bail — and learns the State will try him on 3 November
excerpt: The morning began with a solidarity Mass at the Cathedral of the Child Jesus. By afternoon the Archbishop of Lusaka had been formally arrested, charged and taken before a magistrate, where he pleaded not guilty. Bail came with sureties, surrendered travel documents — and, by Tuesday morning, reports that he was still in custody while the paperwork was done.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Solidarity, condemnation and a call for calm: Zambia absorbs the arrest of an archbishop
excerpt: The bishops spoke of dignity and due process. The opposition spoke of persecution. The State spoke of evidence. And somewhere between the three, a country that has been arguing about its institutions all year found the argument distilled into a single courtroom.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: While Lusaka watched a courtroom, the President landed in Abu Dhabi — and Haimbe told the UN that Zambia is stable and open
excerpt: Day one of the UAE working visit puts a bilateral meeting, MoUs and an investment forum on the President's schedule. In New York, the foreign minister has already delivered the companion message: constitutionalism intact, Human Rights Council candidacy live, and the Grow Zambia Agenda open for partners.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Off the streets by today: Lusaka's vendors face the council's deadline — and a market system that must now absorb them
excerpt: The Lusaka City Council's directive ordering street vendors back into designated markets takes effect today, with non-compliant traders warned they could lose their allocated spaces altogether. Enforcement will be watched block by block — and so will the question of whether the markets have room.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Thirty-six hours and no word: the fuel-tax waiver enters its final day-and-a-half, and the October price review waits on a signature
excerpt: No statutory instrument, no ministerial statement, no gazette — as of this morning, the excise holiday and VAT zero-rating that have subsidised every litre since April still die at midnight tomorrow. The ERB's October review is being assembled in that silence.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Nineteen forty-nine and holding: the kwacha drifts into the fuel decision on a copper tailwind
excerpt: The local unit closed last week stronger and opened this one around K19.49 to the dollar — nearly 19 per cent firmer than a year ago. In a week when the fuel cushion may lapse, the exchange rate is the one variable in the pump-price formula still working for the consumer.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Possession, suspicion and a satisfactory account: what Section 319 actually requires the State to prove against Archbishop Banda
excerpt: The charge against the Archbishop is one of the Penal Code's most unusual offences — it turns not on theft, but on an explanation. With trial set for 3 November, here is what the prosecution must establish, what the defence is likely to argue, and why the five-year-old paper trail of a blue Hilux matters more than the politics around it.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Twenty-one human cases in Muchinga, a ministry correction in Southern — and 600,000 vaccine doses moving: inside Zambia's anthrax response
excerpt: The active front of the outbreak is the Munyamadzi river system in Mpika, where human cases keep ticking up and hippo carcasses keep surfacing. In Southern Province, the government has spent a week knocking down a scarier number. Both stories say something about how the country handles a zoonosis it has met before.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: Six o'clock in Ndola: a winless streak, a quiet coach's promise and the night that decides what this qualifying campaign is
excerpt: Zambia host Togo at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium at 18:00 CAT — bottom of Group I against joint-top, nine matches without a win, and a coach who says the table can still be changed. By 20:00, the campaign has either restarted or gone very quiet.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The rigs are up, the sponsors are in, the Golden Circle is gone: Lusaka counts down to Derulo Saturday
excerpt: With four days to the Stanbic Music Festival, silver sponsors are still signing on, the organisers' tiers are selling through, and the city's showgrounds economy is in its busiest week of the year. Saturday at Polo Field A is now a test of demand as much as a concert.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: Mass at eight, the DEC at ten: Archbishop Banda answers a renewed summons over a five-year-old Hilux — and the Church walks him to the door
excerpt: The Catholic Archbishop of Lusaka is due before Drug Enforcement Commission investigators this morning, nine months after he was warned and cautioned — and stayed silent — in the same investigation. The case is a Toyota Hilux once registered to the Zambia Revenue Authority. The context is a country arguing about whether its institutions are being turned on its critics.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'Speaking out is citizenship, not rebellion': Brian Matambo's 31-minute reckoning with five years of looking away
excerpt: In a Sunday video address accompanying a documentary titled 'Silence Brought Us Here', the Tonse Alliance figure traces a line from the peaceful 2021 handover to the treason arrests of 2026 — and tells Zambians the boundary moved because nobody pushed back.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Abu Dhabi tomorrow, New York today: Hichilema takes the Grow Zambia pitch to the Gulf as Haimbe addresses the UN
excerpt: The President begins a two-day working visit to the UAE on Tuesday — bilateral talks, MoUs and an investment forum on the agenda — hours after his foreign minister delivers Zambia's national statement to the UN General Assembly in New York.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'What message is he sending to the younger generation?': Chief Choongo rebukes Dr Kalumba — and explains why chiefs stand with the government of the day
excerpt: The Monze traditional leader and former House of Chiefs chairperson calls the former minister's remarks about the President disappointing and un-Zambian, telling a country deep in a quarrel about dissent that the campaign season is over.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: One day of relief left: the fuel-tax waiver dies at midnight tomorrow, Lusaka has said nothing — and the October price review is already in the room
excerpt: The excise-duty holiday and VAT zero-rating that have subsidised every litre since April lapse on 30 September. No statutory instrument has been gazetted, no minister has spoken, and the ERB's October review — due within days — will be the first to price fuel without knowing whether the cushion exists.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Copper declared as cement: Avocado Mining admits attempted smuggling — and its K100,000 fine falls due the day after tomorrow
excerpt: The Kalulushi-based miner pleaded guilty to ten counts over a 2025 attempt to export K23.9 million of copper concentrate labelled as Portland cement. In a separate operation, ZRA seized two brand-new Land Cruisers misclassified at the border — a Sunday statement that reads as a warning shot to the whole clearing trade.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Candles at the Cancer Diseases Hospital: September closes with a vigil — and a survival target Zambia has four years to meet
excerpt: At a Friday evening vigil marking Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, the Ministry of Health put the country's position plainly: about 400,000 children worldwide develop cancer each year, most in low- and middle-income countries — and Zambia has promised to help push survival to 60 per cent by 2030.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: Bronze for the juniors, a three-peat for Amajita: Zambia leave Maputo with a medal as South Africa take the crown again
excerpt: Gift Mumbi and a Sipho Muntanga double beat Namibia 3-0 in Sunday's third-place play-off, before South Africa retained the regional title 2-1 against the hosts — a fifth straight win that sends both finalists to Ghana 2027, and sends Zambia home with pride intact but no ticket.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The eve of the must-win: a recovery session, a quiet stadium and a Tuesday night that could define the qualifying campaign
excerpt: Twenty-four hours before Togo arrive at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, Zambia's squad is managing its wounds from Algeria and the federation is still selling tickets. The table is not complicated: the visitors are level at the top, the hosts are bottom, and November's fixtures get very dark if Tuesday goes wrong.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Golden Circle gone, Saturday looms: Jason Derulo comes to the Polo Field — and Lusaka's big-show economy takes another step
excerpt: The Stanbic Music Festival returns on 3 October with its biggest headline booking yet: Jason Derulo, one night only, at Polo Field A. Golden Circle tickets are already sold out — VIP and standard remain — in a week that has made Lusaka's international concert calendar feel suddenly permanent.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: Twenty-nine days, one court bus, no plea: Mundubile and Zulu surface in Solwezi — and the case against them starts to take shape
excerpt: Zambia's defeated presidential candidate and his running mate made their first court appearance since their August arrest, ferried across the country from Kabwe to face sedition charges over post-election Facebook posts. The treason case that jailed them has yet to reach a courtroom at all.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Arrested at dawn in Chienge, charged in Kabwe, bonded by evening: the two-day case against Dr Katele Kalumba
excerpt: The former finance minister faces a cyber-harassment charge over an August post said to humiliate the President. The opposition calls the manner of his arrest an abduction; the ruling party says a man pardoned out of prison by this President should know better.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'What is this hullabaloo?': Hichilema says there is no crisis — and tells social media they are scaring away the investors he fought to win
excerpt: At a routine swearing-in on Friday the President delivered anything but a routine speech: a defence of the post-election climate, a warning that the law 'does not recognise age', and an appeal to Zambians at home and abroad to stop 'creating a crisis where there is none'.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Six passports cancelled, one seven-day ultimatum: Haimbe defends the exile-list from New York as Mutambo's lawyers count down to Monday
excerpt: The Foreign Affairs Minister says withdrawing a passport is not withdrawing citizenship; the UK-based commentator's lawyers say the cancellation was unlawful, attributed to the wrong official and unexplained beyond two words: 'security reasons'. Court action is threatened if it is not restored within days.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The cushion expires on Tuesday: government still undecided on fuel-tax relief as the October price review looms
excerpt: Since April, suspended excise duty and zero-rated VAT have quietly subsidised every litre sold in Zambia — at a cost of roughly $200 million a quarter in forgone revenue. The relief lapses on 30 September, and as of this weekend, Lusaka had not said whether it will be renewed.
author: Natasha Banda

title: 'Two-way impact': Zambia takes its Human Rights Council campaign to New York, with its record very much in the room
excerpt: At a reception for UN member states, the President and his foreign minister asked the world to elect Zambia to the Human Rights Council for 2027–2029 — a bid that lands in the same week as an EU resolution on post-election repression and a defence of six cancelled passports.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'Togo won't have it easy': home, hurt and already cornered — Lwandamina's Chipolopolo reach the must-win in Ndola
excerpt: Back from Tizi Ouzou with a 3-1 defeat, a bruised squad and a blunt table — Zambia bottom, Togo level with Algeria at the top — the interim coach is asking the Levy Mwanawasa crowd to turn one match into a rescue operation on Tuesday night.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: One more morning in Maputo: Junior Chipolopolo play for bronze today as South Africa and Mozambique contest the crown
excerpt: Two days after the 4-2 semi-final that slipped away, Zambia's youngsters face Namibia in the third-place play-off at ABB Stadium — a consolation match that doubles as an audition — before the hosts meet the holders for the regional title and the two Ghana 2027 tickets already booked.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Number 10 in Denmark: Mercy Chipasula, 18, takes the Copper Queens pipeline to HB Køge
excerpt: The Kitwe-born forward who captained Zambia's U17s and has already played two senior WAFCONs has signed for the Danish top-flight club — whose sporting director says they beat 'some of the biggest clubs in the world' to her signature.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The gates are open: Zambia's national parks are free to enter this weekend — and today is the last day
excerpt: To mark World Tourism Day, the Ministry of Tourism waived entry fees at all 20 national parks on 26 and 27 September for citizens and school groups — a two-day invitation to see the estate the country keeps selling to the world.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: 'Resist it': Laura Miti's third-term warning lands as Chapter One tells the President to say it plainly
excerpt: Two of civil society's loudest voices moved within a day of each other — one telling Zambians to resist any third-term push before it starts, the other telling Hakainde Hichilema that only his own words can end the speculation.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'A full-blown police state': Kateka says the security wings are being used to silence dissent — and claims the clampdown was planned before the vote
excerpt: The New Heritage Party leader used a radio interview to accuse the UPND of winning 'with manipulation' and deploying the army where it had lost — claims the government has consistently rejected, and which observer missions have not substantiated.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Healing as homework: church leaders tell a divided country to pray — and to reconcile
excerpt: At the Revival Prayer Network's Grand Thursday gathering in Lusaka, three church figures framed post-election reconciliation as the Church's assignment — not the state's alone.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 6.1 per cent: inflation grinds to an eight-year low — five days before the fuel-tax cushion expires
excerpt: ZamStats' September print extends the disinflation run that returned the rate to the Bank of Zambia's 6–8 per cent band in February — but the monthly figure is the firmest in five months, and the tax measures cushioning fuel lapse on Tuesday.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Borrowing from the funeral grant, at zero per cent: 7,000 retirees have drawn K90 million from NAPSA's advance
excerpt: The facility pays up to 75 per cent of a retiree's funeral grant while they are still alive — recovered in small deductions so the monthly pension keeps coming. Demand, says CEO Muyangwa Muyangwa, is growing daily.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Sixteen and a half thousand new cancers a year: the Cancer Diseases Hospital puts a number on the burden
excerpt: Cervical cancer alone accounts for about 4,700 new cases annually and kills more than half of those it strikes, UTH's cancer hospital says — with only about 3,000 patients currently in treatment there.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: 'The soil was loose and dangerous': a warned-off scramble for copper stones kills three illegal miners at KCM's OB-19 dump
excerpt: Two teenagers and a 20-year-old died when a section of the Chingola dumpsite collapsed on Wednesday evening. Five were pulled out alive by fellow miners. Police have opened an inquiry — and repeated a familiar Copperbelt warning.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Sakala's riposte, then the desert cold: Zambia fall 3-1 in Tizi Ouzou as the winless run reaches nine
excerpt: Fashion Sakala's 57th-minute equaliser briefly quietened the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium, but Ibrahim Maza and Anis Hadj Moussa struck inside seven second-half minutes to give Ibrahim Hamdani a winning start — and leave Chipolopolo bottom of the group. Togo visit on Tuesday.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: A lead, an equaliser, a red card, two penalties: Junior Chipolopolo's AFCON dream dies in a 4-2 Maputo classic
excerpt: Zambia led holders South Africa at half-time and levelled again at 2-2 through Jonathan Kalimina — who was sent off moments later. Steven Mendes scored twice from the spot, Emile Witbooi sealed it late, and the 12-time champions miss out on Ghana 2027.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: 'Take them to court or release them — you can't have it both ways': Laura Miti's ultimatum over the Kafwaya silence
excerpt: A month after former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya died in a security operation, one of the country's best-known rights campaigners says the state's silence has left it exposed to the conclusion it fears most — an unlawful killing.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: 'Beacon of democracy', with an asterisk: EU promises Zambia deeper ties and €110 million — and presses the rule of law
excerpt: Commissioner Jozef Síkela's bilateral with Mulambo Haimbe in New York delivered budget support, a Global Gateway embrace and diplomatic relations with Andorra — while Brussels kept one eye on Kabwe.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The petition that ended with a handshake: Mwewa confirmed as Lusaka mayor after Kibombwe consents to withdraw
excerpt: The Local Government Elections Tribunal has formally withdrawn Gabriel Kibombwe's challenge to the 13 August mayoral result — by the mutual consent of every party in the room — ending a month of legal shadow over City Hall.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Zanaco writes the rulebook: Zambia's first bank sustainability bond heads to market at $100 million
excerpt: A $50 million private placement anchored by British International Investment's $15 million opens the programme — a transaction the Lusaka Securities Exchange calls a first for a Zambian bank, and a template it hopes others will copy.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Four hundred chemical engineers wanted: CBU and UCF sign lab deal ahead of a $1.5 billion fertiliser expansion
excerpt: United Capital Fertilisers will help build a state-of-the-art chemical laboratory, lecture theatre and student accommodation at the Copperbelt University — and says its ammonia-urea plant expansion breaks ground within weeks.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Forty-six dead hippos, one confirmed case: what we actually know about the Muchinga anthrax outbreak
excerpt: Laboratory evidence is lagging the carcass count in the Munyamadzi corridor. Zambia's national One Health coordinator says only one hippo death is lab-confirmed — and cautions against blaming anthrax for every dead animal.
author: Lusaka Brief Health Desk

title: Matchday in Tizi Ouzou: Chipolopolo open the road to AFCON 2027 against the Desert Foxes tonight
excerpt: A rebuilt Zambia squad — completed by the late arrivals of Lungu and Liteta, and minus the withdrawn Andrew Sinkala — faces Algeria at the Hussein Aït Ahmed Stadium with a long winless run to snap.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Ninety minutes from Ghana: Junior Chipolopolo meet holders South Africa with an AFCON ticket on the line
excerpt: Friday's 16:00 CAT semi-final in Maputo pits the region's two most decorated youth sides against each other — Zambia's twelve titles against Amajita's ten — with the finalists bound for the U20 AFCON in Ghana.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Silondwa survives three-way countback to lift Discover Insurance golf title at Nkana
excerpt: Kedrick Silondwa's 42 points off a 12 handicap topped a tightly contested field at Nkana Golf Club, as the insurer marked its fourth anniversary with the championship.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The gate at Mukobeko stays shut: treason accused cut off from visitors as defence demands answers
excerpt: Prison officers in Kabwe have turned away visitors to Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused, according to people familiar with the attempts — the latest front in a case where procedure has become the story.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: 'Our diplomacy must help to grow Zambia': Haimbe works the UN corridors as two stories compete outside
excerpt: Two new diplomatic relationships, a Human Rights Council bid and a national statement on Monday — while diaspora organisers and the foreign minister tell different stories about protests at the gates.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 'Two terms': the opposition is quoting Hichilema back at himself as the term-limits storm swirls
excerpt: State House has repeatedly denied any third-term ambition. But with Tayali's campaign growing louder and the President yet to address it directly this week, his own past words have become the opposition's favourite document.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The kwacha at 19.5, inflation at an eight-year low: a week of deadlines for Zambia's economic managers
excerpt: The currency has drifted softly this month while prices stay tame. Now three dates collide — the September inflation print, a monetary policy decision and the expiry of the fuel-tax moratorium.
author: Natasha Banda

title: KCM signs $498m deal to mine its own waste — the biggest tailings recovery plant in Africa
excerpt: Vedanta's Zambian unit will extract 70,000 tonnes of copper a year from decades of Chingola tailings, as the metal's price and the country's three-million-tonne ambition keep climbing.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Twenty-two games unbeaten: Belmadi's Algeria await the Chipolopolo in Tizi Ouzou
excerpt: George Lwandamina's first competitive match in charge is about as hard as African football gets — away to the Desert Foxes on Friday night, with Togo at home four days later.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Three wins, eight goals, one conceded: Junior Chipolopolo sweep Group C and meet the hosts on Friday
excerpt: A 3-1 win over Botswana sealed a perfect group stage in Maputo. One more win — against Mozambique in the semi-final — puts Zambia at the Under-20 AFCON in Ghana.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The season of the stage: Stanbic festival returns as Kwacha Music Awards locks in November
excerpt: Zambia's live-music calendar is stacking up — a bank-backed festival promising a star-studded local lineup, and the industry's biggest night set for 27 November.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: 'No cousin, no brother': Hichilema swears in his second-term cabinet with a warning
excerpt: President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn in the first batch of his new cabinet at State House, telling ministers that delivery — not relationships — will decide who keeps their seat.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Treason case: Correctional Service denies blocking lawyers as Findlay's family raises health alarm
excerpt: A dispute has erupted over legal access at Mukobeko — while Harry Findlay's family says his health is deteriorating in detention.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Tonse Alliance suspends Zimba — the dialogue call that cost him his job
excerpt: Days after urging the opposition to recognise President Hichilema and pursue dialogue, secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has been suspended.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Mwamba demands independent probe into officer's death at police headquarters
excerpt: The Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance disputes the police account that Assistant Superintendent Daniel Banda took his own life.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kenya signs for 540,000 tonnes of Zambian maize — the record harvest finds its market
excerpt: The Food Reserve Agency has signed with Kenya's Baita Trading to export more than half a million tonnes of surplus maize.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Inflation eases to 9.2% as food prices stabilise — relief, with a footnote
excerpt: The disinflation run continues toward single digits. The market stall will confirm when it arrives.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Hichilema presses Vedanta to fast-track power investment as copper ambitions outrun the grid
excerpt: The president has urged Vedanta to accelerate power-generation plans, as fresh GreenCo funding signals the private build-out is moving.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Anthrax scare in Muchinga: what is confirmed, what is ruled out
excerpt: Suspected anthrax recorded in Muchinga Province; Lavushimanda reports no livestock cases. What the evidence says so far.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Barbra Banda nominated for the Ballon d'Or — again
excerpt: The Copper Queens and Orlando Pride striker is on the Ballon d'Or shortlist for another year.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Al Merrikh in Ndola as Power Dynamos chase a CAF comeback
excerpt: Zambian champions Power Dynamos host Sudanese giants Al Merrikh needing to overturn a first-leg deficit.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Hichilema sworn in for a second term — and the economy is the whole speech
excerpt: Hakainde Hichilema took the oath at National Heroes Stadium on Tuesday after winning 61.4% of the vote. His promise for term two: investment, jobs, and three times the copper.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and Findlay moved to Mukobeko as treason case widens to 18
excerpt: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu and businessman Harry Findlay have been transferred to Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison on treason charges, according to multiple reports.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Zumani Zimba breaks ranks: 'Zambia must choose dialogue over division'
excerpt: Tonse Alliance secretary general Dr Chris Zumani Zimba has defied critics within his own camp to call for national dialogue — and even a government of national unity.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: The kwacha is one of 2026's standout currencies. What does that buy you?
excerpt: Up roughly 20% against the dollar in a year and trading near 19.1 to the greenback, the kwacha is riding copper and a record maize harvest.
author: Natasha Banda

title: September 30 is copper day: the export-duty decision that reveals Zambia's real bottleneck
excerpt: Zambia extended its waiver on the 10% copper-concentrate export duty to the end of September while the country's biggest smelters sit in maintenance.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Zambia's copper boom runs on electricity the grid doesn't have yet
excerpt: Reaching 3 million tonnes of copper needs at least 2,000 extra megawatts. The power deficit was 707MW last year — but Kariba is recovering.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Fuel prices hold for September — and it's the suspended taxes doing the work
excerpt: Petrol stays at K25.29 and diesel at K26.86 despite Middle East pressure on oil prices.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Zesco Ndola Girls' COSAFA run ends in final defeat — 'we'll be back for the title'
excerpt: A perfect group stage, a semi-final statement, then Mamelodi Sundowns in the final. Zesco Ndola Girls fell short — but announced themselves.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Kangwa's Greek move and Lungu's injury race: the Chipolopolo European watch
excerpt: Klings Kangwa unveiled by Panathinaikos after a Hall of Fame farewell, while Gamphani Lungu races an injury before AFCON preparations.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Kopala showed up for Danny Kaya — and Lusaka got its turn this weekend
excerpt: The eighth Danny Kaya Music Festival packed the Copperbelt before a moving tribute to the late Dandy Krazy.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk

title: Veteran Refinery shutdown: what is confirmed, what is claimed, and what remains unanswered
excerpt: The Copperbelt facility has halted operations under disputed circumstances. Allegations about the arrest of Mr. D. Nayek remain unverified.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Inflation falls to 6.5% — the lowest in eight years
excerpt: Zambia's annual inflation rate eased to 6.5% in June 2026, a level last seen in February 2018, as the kwacha firmed and debt restructuring steadied the economy.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Justice minister moves to defer Bill 7 again
excerpt: The Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Bill No. 7 was deferred once more in late June, with the Justice Ministry citing the need for further consultation on the divisive constitutional package.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema launches UPND manifesto: growth, jobs, free education
excerpt: President Hichilema formally launched his re-election platform on 11 June, promising continued economic recovery, expanded free education and support for agriculture.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kwacha touches 18 to the dollar — strongest in nearly three years
excerpt: The kwacha firmed to around K18.07 per US dollar in June, its strongest level since 2023, buoyed by copper earnings, reserves at about US$6.5 billion and renewed investor confidence.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema switches on Chisamba II: 100 more megawatts of solar
excerpt: The US$70 million second phase of the Chisamba solar plant was commissioned on 21 July, doubling the site to 200MW — a centrepiece of the drought-proofing energy push.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: The reserves row: US$6.5 billion in the bank, and a campaign over who feels it
excerpt: A debate over Zambia's record foreign-exchange reserves became the economic heart of the campaign, with Brian Mundubile asking what US$6.5 billion does for the cost of living — and Situmbeko Musokotwane answering.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: The burial that became a campaign: Lungu's legacy shadows the race
excerpt: A year after his death, the unresolved burial of former president Edgar Lungu has become one of the most emotive issues of the campaign, after Brian Mundubile promised a 'dignified burial' if elected.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Copper Queens wrap up pre-camp as preparations intensify
excerpt: Zambia's women's national team concluded a local pre-camp in July as the technical team steps up preparations, with attention on the next generation joining the Barbra Banda core.
author: Lusaka Brief Sports Desk

title: Election day: 8.7 million registered voters go to the polls
excerpt: Zambians voted on 13 August to choose a president, 226 constituency MPs, mayors and councillors — a vote framed as a referendum on the government's economic record.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Hichilema wins a second term with about 60% of the vote
excerpt: The Electoral Commission declared Hakainde Hichilema re-elected with about 60.5% of the vote against Brian Mundubile's 37.9%, while the UPND took a commanding parliamentary majority.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Kabulonga operation: former minister Kafwaya killed, opposition figures detained
excerpt: A security operation at a Lusaka property days after the vote left former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya dead in what police described as an exchange of fire, and led to the detention of senior opposition figures — including, reportedly, Brian Mundubile found at the scene.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Inflation dips again to 6.2% — closing in on the target floor
excerpt: Annual inflation eased to 6.2% in August, a new eight-year low, with mealie meal prices falling month-on-month — welcome data for a re-elected government with promises to keep.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Lusaka rejects EU Parliament's post-election resolution as 'premature'
excerpt: The European Parliament has called for an independent investigation into the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya and the post-election crackdown. Government says the resolution is premature and insufficiently informed.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others sue the State over their detention
excerpt: The eighteen treason suspects have petitioned over alleged rights violations, saying they were moved from Mukobeko to Mwembeshi without a lawful warrant — the first major legal counterattack since the charges were laid.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Mafinga South MP Faith Munthali critically ill after alleged abduction
excerpt: The newly elected MP is in Isoka General Hospital after what her family and party describe as an abduction. Police have been asked to investigate; details remain thin and contested.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mpundu accuses Tembo of betrayal as cracks widen in the Tonse Alliance
excerpt: Tonse Alliance chairman Binwell Mpundu has publicly accused Ezra Tembo of betraying those who built his career — the loudest rupture yet inside the opposition since the August defeat.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Former Education PS Henry Tukombe arrested over US$401 million contract
excerpt: Anti-corruption officers have arrested the former Ministry of Education permanent secretary in connection with a US$401 million contract — one of the largest figures ever attached to a Zambian graft case.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Honeybee case reopens: court clears DPP's appeal against Chilufya acquittal
excerpt: The Economic and Financial Crimes Court has ruled the Director of Public Prosecutions' appeal against the acquittal of former health minister Chitalu Chilufya in the Honeybee defective-drugs case can proceed.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Hichilema hosts the Duchess of Edinburgh as royal visit spotlights education
excerpt: President Hichilema met Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, during her visit to Zambia — a diplomatic bright spot in a month dominated by post-election tension.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Mass anthrax vaccination targets 20,000 animals in Muchinga
excerpt: Government has launched a vaccination campaign covering 20,000 animals in Mpika, Shiwang'andu and Lavushimanda, with Mpika identified as the epicentre of the outbreak.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Daka double douses the Flames: Zambia 2-0 Malawi
excerpt: Substitute Billy Daka came off the bench to score twice in the closing stages as the Chipolopolo beat Malawi — a statement win in front of home fans.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Arrows stun Power Dynamos to lift the Charity Shield
excerpt: Red Arrows upset league champions Power Dynamos to win the season-opening Charity Shield — an early marker in what promises to be a fierce title race.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: The term-limits storm: Tayali wants the ceiling scrapped — civil society says don't you dare
excerpt: Calls to scrap the presidential two-term limit have exploded into the open, with Chilufya Tayali leading the charge and civil society, opposition figures and a veteran constitutionalist warning of a third-term agenda.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: Diaspora to protest at the UN as Haimbe arrives to defend Zambia's record
excerpt: Zambians in the US plan a demonstration outside UN headquarters in New York this week over the disputed election and the killing of Mutotwe Kafwaya — days before Foreign Minister Haimbe delivers Zambia's national statement.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: Masebo challenges Chongwe East result over alleged malpractice
excerpt: Losing UPND candidate Sylvia Masebo has petitioned the Lusaka High Court over the Chongwe East parliamentary result — one of a string of election petitions now testing the 13 August outcomes.
author: Chanda Mwape

title: 40 PR MPs sworn in as parliament widens — and watchdogs like what they see
excerpt: Speaker Nelly Mutti has sworn in the 40 proportional-representation members reserved for women, youth and persons with disabilities — the first fruit of the amended constitution's new architecture.
author: Lusaka Brief Newsroom

title: More buyers eye Zambian maize as the record harvest goes to market
excerpt: Regional demand is lining up for Zambia's surplus maize weeks after the 540,000-tonne Kenya deal — with the FRA insisting food security is ring-fenced before exports move.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Lusaka, Copperbelt and Eastern top syphilis infections, health data shows
excerpt: New figures put the three most urbanised provinces at the top of the syphilis burden, with health officials urging testing and early treatment — especially in antenatal care.
author: Natasha Banda

title: Lungu and Liteta complete the squad as Chipolopolo eye Algeria
excerpt: Gamphani Lungu and Liteta have arrived in camp to complete the Chipolopolo squad for the Algeria clash, though German-based Andrew Sinkala has been excused by FAZ.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Haalubono handed the Copper Queens reins for the Olympic battle
excerpt: The Copper Queens have a new head coach as the federation turns its attention to the Olympic qualification campaign — a promotion from within for a programme that plans long cycles.
author: Mwelwa Phiri

title: Short film, long shadow: Lusaka's festival wraps a breakout edition
excerpt: The Lusaka Short Film Festival has concluded after screenings that drew new audiences to Zambian storytelling — another marker for a film scene building real momentum.
author: Lusaka Brief Culture Desk
